stem: A child presents with watery diarrhea and a calculated stool osmotic gap of $120 \text{ mOsm/kg}$. Which clinical feature is most likely associated with this finding?

options.text: The diarrhea stops when the child is placed nil by mouth (fasting).
The diarrhea continues at the same volume even during fasting.
Stool microscopy shows a high concentration of leukocytes and red cells.
The stool pH is likely neutral or slightly alkaline.

explanation: An osmotic gap greater than $100$ indicates osmotic diarrhea, which typically resolves when the ingestion of the non-absorbed solute ceases.
rationale: Recall how the presence or absence of oral intake affects different types of watery diarrhea.

optionExplanations.A: An osmotic gap greater than $100$ indicates osmotic diarrhea, which typically resolves when the ingestion of the non-absorbed solute ceases.
optionExplanations.B: This pattern is characteristic of secretory diarrhea, which is associated with an osmotic gap of less than $50$.
optionExplanations.C: Leukocytes and red cells are markers of inflammation or colitis, rather than a simple osmotic imbalance.
optionExplanations.D: Osmotic diarrhea caused by carbohydrate malabsorption usually results in acidic stools due to bacterial fermentation.
